messages:
maria: Quick follow-up on the continuous-batcher RFC — thinking about moving from a single global queue to 'scheduling islands' per model-shard with token-affinity routing. reduces HOL blocking but adds routing complexity. anyone see immediate red flags?
alex: I like islanding for isolation. main risk is uneven utilization across islands causing wasted capacity.
jamal: yep — starvation is my top worry. if one island gets a fat prompt stream it could soak GPU without global fairness.
sophia: can we do a soft-share budget? each island gets min_guarantee + burstable global pool. enforce via admission tokens.
maria: agreed. admission tokens sounded promising in the RFC, but we need a cheap way to move tokens between islands without global coordination on hot path.
alex: what about token-leasing with periodic reconciliation? lease locally for N ms, return unused tokens to a global pool in background.
jamal: that helps. but we also need preemption for long-running requests — maybe a priority-based evict where small requests can cut into big ones when latency SLOs are in danger.
sophia: preemption is tricky with KV-cache for autoregressive models. evicting a request mid-generation loses cache progress. we could instead do speculative cloning onto spare capacity for high-priority requests. expensive though.
infra-bot: deploy-batcher-sim started: run id b-sim-2026-03-18-07; results in ~10m. will post metrics when ready.
maria: nice. for caching issues, consider 'progress checkpoints' where a long request periodically checkpoints KV-state to allow resume on another worker — only if model supports cheap snapshot.
alex: snapshotting adds memory and serialization cost; we'd want it opt-in per model-version. could be a config: 
```json
{"islands": 16, "affinity_window": 64, "merge_threshold_pct": 30, "checkpoint_interval_ms": 2000}
```
jamal: merge_threshold idea: if island utilization < threshold for Xs, merge into shared queue to improve packing. need hysteresis to avoid flip-flop.
sophia: also track per-island latency percentiles and token churn. eviction or merging decisions should be based on a small vector: {q_depth, p95_lat, token_rate}.
maria: agree. also want cheap signals for backpressure exposed to clients: HTTP 429 with a reason like `island_busy` vs `global_rate_limit`. helps app-level retries.
alex: +1. clients can prefer eventual lower-latency by retrying to a different region/model-variant. we should surface recommended retry-after headers.
jamal: one more: admission policy language should live in config so we can A/B different strategies without deploys. small DSL or JSON schema.
sophia: operational questions — how do we observe islanding effectiveness? need dashboards: island utilization heatmap, cross-island imbalances, merge events, preemption counts.
infra-bot: sim results posted: b-sim-2026-03-18-07: islands=16 baseline shows 12% fewer tokens/sec wasted, p95 tail improved for mixed workloads. full logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/b-sim-2026-03-18-07
maria: good signal. next steps: prototype token-lease + merge controller in the sim, add checkpoint opt-in, and draft follow-up RFC with config schema and observability plan. volunteers?
alex: I can take the token-lease simulation and basic docs.
jamal: I'll do the merge-controller sim and metrics dashboard sketch.
sophia: I'll explore checkpoint API and model compatibility matrix.
maria: perfect. I'll start the RFC draft and link your PRs. thanks all :thumbsup:
